subject: Seasonal SLA pilot: pricing for traffic spikes & escalation coverage
messages:
From: Sara Park <sara@cloudwave.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Cho <alan.cho@cloudwave.com>, Cloudwave Procurement <procurement@cloudwave.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: pilot SLA for seasonal traffic spikes

Hi Sergio —

Hope you’re well. Cloudwave runs a large holiday promotion window each year (late Nov–Dec) and we’re evaluating vendors for a small pilot this fall to validate cost and reliability under burst traffic. Two asks upfront:

1) Can you propose a short-term SLA package that covers predictable seasonal spikes (we expect up to 3x baseline QPS for 2–3 week windows)?
2) What escalation coverage and credit model do you offer if we hit availability or latency targets during the spike?

We’re not ready to commit to Dedicated capacity yet; looking for a pilot pricing model (4–6 weeks) and clear escalation SLAs that map to our internal oncall. If you can include a simple baseline vs. surge pricing table and any pilot discounts or credits, that’d be ideal.

Alan is copied — he handles procurement and will coordinate contracts.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Park
Head of Platform Operations
Cloudwave

---

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Alan Cho <alan.cho@cloudwave.com>, Cloudwave Procurement <procurement@cloudwave.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: pilot SLA for seasonal traffic spikes

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the context — this is exactly the kind of use case we designed Redwood’s pilot packages for. High-level proposal attached (PDF) and a baseline metrics workbook. Quick summary here:

- Pilot duration: 6 weeks (2 weeks warm-up, 3 weeks spike window, 1 week wrap-up)
- Pricing: blended reserved + surge buffer. We provide a small reserved pool sized to your baseline, plus a capped burst pool for spikes. Billing is consumption-based for burst tokens with a negotiated surge cap.
- Credits: service credit tiers tied to availability and p50/p95 token latency during the spike window. If availability drops below the agreed band we offer prorated credits; for latency regressions we provide technical triage + credits.
- Escalation: 24/7 pager covered by Redwood for P1s during spike window; a named escalation lead and a weekly runbook sync.

Next steps I propose: 1) Review the attached proposal, 2) we do a 30-minute scoping call this week to confirm baseline sizing, 3) iterate on a one-page pilot SOW for Alan/procurement.

I’ve looped in Marissa for pricing and Karthik for escalation ops.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-seasonal-sla-pilot-proposal.pdf (PDF); pilot-metrics-baseline.xlsx (XLSX)
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Inquiry: pilot SLA for seasonal traffic spikes

Sergio / Karthik —

Draft notes after a quick skim of Cloudwave’s ask and our proposal:

- Pricing mechanic suggestion: a 30% pilot discount on burst units for first pilot, capped at $25k. This lowers their risk and lets us observe real surge patterns.
- Surge cap design: bill burst units at base burst rate up to 2x baseline. Beyond 2x up to 3x, apply a stepped premium (1.25x) but include a one-time surge credit if they hit >2.5x and we fail the latency SLO.
- Credits: availability credit as % of pilot invoice (3% per 1% below SLA, capped at 30%). For latency regressions, provide a 10% invoice credit + dedicated remediation hours.
- Operational ask: Karthik, can we commit to an on-call rotation for P1s during spike weeks and a named technical lead for postmortem?

I’ll prep a short concessions table for procurement. Sergio — want me to push this into the PDF and send back to Cloudwave or do you want to stay as point?

Marissa
Sr. Pricing & Decks
Redwood Inference
From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@cloudwave.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Park <sara@cloudwave.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Cloudwave Procurement <procurement@cloudwave.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: pilot SLA for seasonal traffic spikes

Thanks Sergio / Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions from procurement before we move to SOW:

1) Can you confirm total cost exposure (example table) if we hit sustained 3x baseline for the 3-week spike? We need an upper-bound for finance.
2) On credits: the availability credit sounds reasonable; we’d prefer latency credits tied to p95 > 600ms rather than a generic latency regression band. Can you map the thresholds?
3) Escalation: we need a named escalation contact and service hours for triage (30min SLA to acknowledge P1).

If you can return an updated one-pager that includes a worst-case cost table and the exact latency thresholds tied to credits, we can route internally and get back with a DocuSign-ready SOW.

Alan
VP, Procurement
Cloudwave

Alan / Sara —

Thanks for the notes — we revised the one-pager and included the worst-case cost example and latency thresholds. Summary of changes:

- Worst-case cost table: shows baseline reserved + burst consumption at sustained 3x for 21 days; absolute upper-bound with 30% pilot discount applied. (See attached PDF.)
- Latency thresholds: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 600ms. Credits apply when p95 > 600ms during spike window: 10% credit on pilot invoice for 600–900ms; 25% credit above 900ms.
- Escalation: named lead for the pilot is Karthik Iyer (karthik@redwood.ai). Acknowledgement SLA for P1s is 30 minutes during spike windows; full remediation target is 4 hours for P1s. We will provide a dedicated on-call pager and weekly runbook syncs.

Next steps: if this looks acceptable, Alan — can you confirm internal routing cadence and whether procurement needs a redline window (we can accept a 72-hour turnaround once the SOW is uploaded to DocuSign)? I’ll share the updated SOW link to the DocuSign record once you confirm.

Best,
Sergio
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
